traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, p. 58), as Opuntia bigelovii: joints 5 to 15 cm long, very turgid, their tubercles about as long as broad; spines numerous and pale yellow, with papery sheaths, their count and length not given.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a trunk of joints 1 to 1.5 m tall with short branches of easily detached joints crowded at its top; lower branches fall away, so the trunk below is bare and dark. Joints 5 to 15 cm long and 3 to 6 cm thick. Pale green to yellow flowers at the joint tips in spring. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge: about a metre within 15 years. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: joints hidden under dense, barbed, straw-yellow spines in papery sheaths that shine silver in back light, darkening to near black on the old trunk. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): its tepals on a spiral (their count by hand: no flora counts them) on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, from the characters of Cactaceae by the rules at the flowering plants. Its 200 stamens by hand, the most a flower draws, for the numerous ones every flora gives.

appearance.bodies.stem.spines.glochid.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, pp. 42 and 57 to 67): the areoles bear glochids above the spines, here not described for the species; the genus's are usually numerous, so drawn pale yellow like its spines. Their count, length and angle are set by eye like a prickly pear's, smaller, as no flora measures them.
